# Drawdown-constrained position sizing under uncertain edge — concept pack

> Source-anchored research for Drawdown-constrained position sizing under uncertain edge. Run status: COMPLETED.

## Vocabulary

Terms this pack was harvested with, grouped by their relation to the concept; counts are units matched / sources. Zero-hit terms are listed under Coverage. On every unit line, `keywords:` names the terms that matched.

- **self**: Drawdown-constrained position sizing under uncertain edge (19/4)

## Structure and components

- [statement] Sun and Boyd’s distributionally robust Kelly method maximizes the smallest expected log growth across a specified set of possible probability distributions. The problem is convex but is not generally tractable; their tractable cases require suitable uncertainty-set structure. This objective addresses distribution uncertainty and does not itself state a hard peak-to-trough drawdown cap. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.10371 · keywords: Drawdown-constrained position sizing under uncertain edge

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] The risk-constrained Kelly model uses nonnegative allocations that sum to one and nonnegative payoff vectors, with cash available. Its stated IID guarantee does not by itself establish a guarantee for leveraged perpetual positions with a different payoff process. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.06183 · keywords: Drawdown-constrained position sizing under uncertain edge
- [statement] In the temporally correlated coin model of O’Brien and colleagues, the finite-horizon optimal constant betting fraction depends on the horizon and startup probability. In their long-run limit it coincides with using the stationary unconditional heads probability in the classical formula. Temporal dependence therefore does not imply a universal leverage haircut. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.02743 · keywords: Drawdown-constrained position sizing under uncertain edge
- [statement] Busseti, Ryu and Boyd report simulation cases where their risk-constrained allocations outperform fractional Kelly at matched drawdown risk or growth. This is a result within their tested models, not a demonstrated superiority on SOL perpetual trading. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.06183 · keywords: Drawdown-constrained position sizing under uncertain edge · also: https://stanford.edu/~boyd/papers/kelly.html
- [statement] The authors’ cvxgrp/kelly_code repository provides code and embedded results for finite-return and infinite-return examples of risk-constrained Kelly. It is an implementation reference for the paper, not evidence of live execution performance. (low confidence) — https://github.com/cvxgrp/kelly_code · keywords: Drawdown-constrained position sizing under uncertain edge
- [statement] The dependence caveat must be scoped to the result: MacLean, Thorp and Ziemba describe maximizing conditional expected log wealth given the past for dependent investments, and Hsieh and Barmish distinguish their dependence-free drawdown lemma from the iid assumption used for their subsequent Kelly optimization example. (medium confidence) — https://www.stat.berkeley.edu/~aldous/157/Papers/Good_Bad_Kelly.pdf · keywords: Drawdown-constrained position sizing under uncertain edge · also: https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.01503

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] In the risk-constrained Kelly model, holding only cash is feasible; it is optimal when all risky bets are losers in expectation. A sizing procedure should therefore allow an abstention outcome rather than force a positive risky allocation. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.06183 · keywords: Drawdown-constrained position sizing under uncertain edge
- [statement] Estimated return distributions can differ from future returns. Sun and Boyd motivate robust sizing by estimation error and distribution shift; MacLean, Thorp and Ziemba recommend reducing wagers because log-growth calculations are sensitive to errors in estimated means. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.10371 · keywords: Drawdown-constrained position sizing under uncertain edge · also: https://www.stat.berkeley.edu/~aldous/157/Papers/Good_Bad_Kelly.pdf
- [statement] A drawdown-dependent controller can reduce exposure as remaining drawdown capacity shrinks. Hsieh and Barmish multiply account value by a gain and a modulator equal to remaining permitted drawdown divided by one minus current drawdown; their formula sets exposure to zero when the drawdown limit is reached. This is a model-conditional control rule rather than evidence of a profitable trading edge. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.01503 · keywords: Drawdown-constrained position sizing under uncertain edge

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Baker and McHale report that shrinking plug-in Kelly bets improves out-of-sample performance in their simulations and tennis-betting analysis. Sun and Boyd independently identify uncertainty between empirical training distributions and future returns as a practical problem for nominal Kelly sizing. These results motivate uncertainty-aware sizing; they do not calibrate a crypto leverage level. (medium confidence) — https://pubsonline.informs.org/doi/10.1287/deca.2013.0271 · keywords: Drawdown-constrained position sizing under uncertain edge · also: https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.10371
- [statement] Distributionally robust Kelly chooses an allocation that maximizes the smallest expected log growth over a specified set of possible distributions. Its protection is relative to that chosen uncertainty set. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.10371 · keywords: Drawdown-constrained position sizing under uncertain edge
- [statement] Sun and Boyd distinguish convexity from tractability: distributionally robust Kelly is convex in principle, but need not be tractable for a general uncertainty set; they derive tractable formulations for useful finite-outcome cases. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.10371 · keywords: Drawdown-constrained position sizing under uncertain edge
- [statement] The drawdown definitions differ materially: Busseti, Ryu and Boyd constrain wealth falling below a fraction of initial wealth, whereas Hsieh and Barmish define percentage drawdown relative to the running account-value peak. These constraints must be specified separately. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/1603.06183v1 · keywords: Drawdown-constrained position sizing under uncertain edge · also: https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.01503, https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.06183
- [statement] For the IID fixed-allocation model of Busseti, Ryu and Boyd, setting λ = log β / log α and imposing E[(rᵀb)^(-λ)] ≤ 1 gives a sufficient bound on the probability that minimum wealth falls below α. Replacing the original drawdown constraint with this condition restricts the feasible set and produces a convex problem. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.06183 · keywords: Drawdown-constrained position sizing under uncertain edge · also: https://arxiv.org/html/1603.06183v1
- [statement] In Hsieh and Barmish, the drawdown modulator scales investment by remaining drawdown capacity relative to remaining wealth. Their admissible feedback gains depend on explicit upper and lower return bounds. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.01503 · keywords: Drawdown-constrained position sizing under uncertain edge
- [statement] Hsieh and Barmish explicitly state that their drawdown-modulation lemma does not require IID returns. It does require explicit realizable return bounds, and their market model assumes zero transaction costs, zero interest rates and perfect liquidity. Those assumptions must be checked before transferring the pathwise guarantee. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.01503 · keywords: Drawdown-constrained position sizing under uncertain edge
- [statement] Baker and McHale support shrinkage for estimation uncertainty in their betting study. Downey’s interactive simulation instead reports only modest sizing changes from random win-probability variation and discusses systematic overestimation and downside objectives. These differently specified uncertainty models do not justify an unconditional rule that uncertainty alone requires half Kelly. (low confidence) — https://pubsonline.informs.org/doi/10.1287/deca.2013.0271 · keywords: Drawdown-constrained position sizing under uncertain edge · also: https://matthewdowney.github.io/uncertainty-kelly-criterion-optimal-bet-size.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com
- [statement] Fractional Kelly scales risky allocations down toward cash and trades lower growth for greater security. It remains exposed to finite-sequence losses; shrinking a Kelly allocation alone does not establish a hard maximum drawdown guarantee. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/1603.06183v1 · keywords: Drawdown-constrained position sizing under uncertain edge · also: https://www.stat.berkeley.edu/~aldous/157/Papers/Good_Bad_Kelly.pdf
- [statement] Hsieh and Barmish’s drawdown-modulation lemma bounds position size using current drawdown, current wealth and explicit return-support bounds. Its drawdown guarantee does not require independent identically distributed returns, but the model assumes bounded returns, zero transaction costs, zero interest rates and perfect liquidity. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.01503 · keywords: Drawdown-constrained position sizing under uncertain edge
